items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: Well, they was doing all the business out there, and I was with Tut. And I stayed with Tut from 24 until 26.

ctx.x: He'd sing a lot of waltzes. And then there was time waltzes was awful popular.

And he'd sing a lot of them. Did a lot of singing. But he didn't play anything. Oh, he had a playhouse in his yard, though. That thing was around 12 by 12 was a little girl. He had a real funny to play. He was a great guy. He was a great guy. for his little girl. They had real furniture in there too, but that was just the playhouse there. He had a wonderful home over there. Well, there was the three leading orchestras outside of New Orleans. It was Bud Scott, Claiborne William, and Tut Johnson. Claiborne William…

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: To Johnson had been after me for about six or eight months to come up and join his band.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. What caused you to leave the band in the end, you know, wouldn't you?

Yes, uh, the music had got slow, things had got kind of, you know, bad. With Tom's band or with all the bands? Yeah, with all the bands, right. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. And I had gotten married then, and, uh, expecting my first child and I needed some money. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. To Johnson had been after me for about six or eight months to come up and join his band. He thought it was a pretty good salary. And, uh, I sit down and talk to Mr. Tom about it. And, uh, he told me I'd be a fool if I didn't go take him. Because he was…
But you were here, you mean, or you were in New Orleans? Yeah, I was in New Orleans. Yeah, yeah.
